headline: A dust storm took the sky out of Kansas in April, Germany stripped Jews of citizenship in September
texture: Black Sunday hit the southern plains on April 14 and the dust rolled east far enough to darken Chicago. Roosevelt signed the Social Security Act on August 14, which set up pensions and unemployment insurance where neither had existed. The Nuremberg Laws came into force on September 15 and removed citizenship from German Jews. Italy invaded Ethiopia on October 2.

Parker Brothers started selling Monopoly on February 6, a game about buying property in a year when almost nobody could. Alcoholics Anonymous was founded in Akron on June 10. Germany began the world's first regular television service on March 22, to an audience of almost nobody, and Roosevelt dedicated the Hoover Dam in September.

Mutiny on the Bounty led the box office and won Best Picture, and MGM had four of the five biggest films. Top Hat came second, which meant Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers dancing through a Depression that was in its sixth year. T. E. Lawrence died on May 19 after a motorcycle crash, and the Chinese Communists ended the Long March in Shaanxi in October.

notes: Research pass July 2026. No prices section: the three price series all start later. The dust reaching Chicago, and Lawrence dying after a motorcycle crash, are general knowledge of those events rather than statements from the year pages, and come out if challenged. The Hoover Dam dedication carries a month because the source gives no day.
